capabilities: Capture the rendered reading view as a long screenshot
Export notes as PDF, JPG or PNG, paginated or as one image
Split long notes into A4, A5, B5, Letter or custom paper sizes with smart page breaks
Insert forced page breaks with /// and adjust break positions in a preview
Add visible or hidden watermarks and author signatures to exported pages
extras: Desktop only (no phones or tablets); requires Obsidian 1.4.0+. Exported PDFs store content as images with no selectable text layer and non-clickable links. Uses direct Node.js filesystem access to write outside the vault, which security scanners may flag. MIT-licensed; includes batch export of a chosen folder and a hidden pixel-level watermark feature.
motivation: The author wanted to export a finished Markdown note to PDF and then to an image for sharing, but found that rendered effects disappeared or changed during export, so a screenshot-first approach was built to preserve the reading view exactly.
problem: Obsidian's PDF export can alter rendered content such as gradients, shadows, formulas, diagrams and custom styling, so the exported file no longer matches what the author sees in reading view.

relations.evidence: For Word or ePub, consider Pandoc.
For PDF links, bookmarks and merging several notes, take a look at Better Export PDF.

summary: Note exporter that captures the rendered reading view as a long screenshot and outputs it as PDF, JPG or PNG, paginated or as one continuous image.
